result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both answers recommend annual as the default while keeping monthly readable, and both suggest tracking refunds, early cancellations and support tickets alongside conversion. A edges ahead with the full arithmetic, including the $65.89 saving and a 'Save $65.89 vs. monthly' line, a concrete fix that puts $12.99/month on the toggle itself, and a quick legibility test. B adds useful detail on WCAG contrast and auto-renewal law and asks a fair clarifying question, but leaves out the dollar saving and makes one slightly unsupported claim ('usually lifts revenue per signup'); A makes a similar unsupported claim that annual surprises are 'the biggest source' of refunds. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): B gives a clearer recommendation and keeps the annual default separate from the problem of making the monthly price hard to read. It also gives the exact $65.89 saving with the math shown and suggests putting $12.99/month on the toggle itself. A is solid and its numbers are correct, but it never states the dollar saving, ties the refund risk to disclosure more than to the grey text, and cites click-to-cancel as a current risk, which is legally shaky.
